stem: A trail mix contains almonds and cashews weighing 3 pounds total. Almonds cost $4 per pound and cashews cost $7 per pound. The total cost of the mix is $15. How many pounds of almonds are in the mix?

distractor_rationales.A: Student set up one equation correctly but used the wrong constraint for total weight
distractor_rationales.C: Student averaged the two pound amounts rather than solving the system
distractor_rationales.D: Student assigned all 3 pounds to almonds, ignoring the cost constraint

solution_steps: Let a = pounds of almonds, c = pounds of cashews
why_this_difficulty: Medium: requires translating two real-world constraints into two equations, then solving by substitution. Students often set up only one equation.

stem: A rectangle has length l feet and width w feet. The equation 2l + 2w = 48 represents the perimeter of the rectangle. The width is 8 feet. What is the length, in feet, of the rectangle?

distractor_rationales.8: Student set length equal to width
distractor_rationales.24: Student divided 48 by 2 and reported that as the length, ignoring width
distractor_rationales.32: Student subtracted only one width: 48 − 8 = 40, then divided by 2 incorrectly

why_this_difficulty: Medium: requires recognising which variable is given, substituting, and solving a one-step linear equation in context.

stem: A phone plan charges a flat monthly fee of $20 plus $0.05 per text message. In one month, Marcus was charged $35. How many text messages did Marcus send that month?

distractor_rationales.A: Student found 35 − 20 = 15 and reported the dollar difference as the count
distractor_rationales.B: Student divided 35 by 0.05 instead of (35 − 20) by 0.05
distractor_rationales.D: Student divided the full $35 by $0.05 instead of the overage only

why_this_difficulty: Medium: two-step equation in context. The most common error is dividing the full amount by the per-unit rate rather than the amount above the flat fee.

stem: In August, a store manager completed 5 more than three times the number of reports completed in September. In the two months combined, 61 reports were completed. How many reports were completed in September?

distractor_rationales.47: Student found the August count instead of September
distractor_rationales.19: Student added 5 to the correct September count instead of computing it
distractor_rationales.56: Student subtracted 5 from 61 and reported that as September

why_this_difficulty: Hard: requires translating 'more than three times' into 3s + 5 correctly (a common mistranslation is 3(s + 5)), then solving and identifying that the question asks for September, not August.

stem: The equation C = 45h + 30 gives the total cost C, in dollars, for a contractor to work h hours on a project, where h ≥ 0. Which of the following is the best interpretation of 45 in this context?

choices.A: The total cost, in dollars, of the project
choices.B: The contractor's hourly rate, in dollars per hour
choices.C: The number of hours worked on the project
choices.D: The one-time setup fee, in dollars, for the project

distractor_rationales.A: Student confused the coefficient with the output value C
distractor_rationales.C: Student confused the coefficient 45 with the variable h
distractor_rationales.D: Student identified the fixed fee correctly as 30 but then misassigned 45 to the same role

solution_steps: In C = 45h + 30, the coefficient of h is the rate of change: cost increases by $45 for each additional hour
30 is the y-intercept: the fixed fee regardless of hours worked
45 is the cost per hour — the hourly rate
why_this_difficulty: Hard: tests interpretation of slope in a linear model. Students must distinguish the rate of change (45) from the y-intercept (30) and translate each into real-world meaning.

stem: A catering company charges \(\$12\) per hot item and \(\$8\) per cold item. For one event, a customer ordered a total of 15 items and was charged \(\$148\). How many hot items did the customer order?

distractor_rationales.A: Student set up the cost equation correctly but made an arithmetic error when solving
distractor_rationales.C: Student swapped hot and cold item counts
distractor_rationales.D: Student found the number of cold items instead of hot items

solution_steps: Let h = hot items, c = cold items
why_this_difficulty: Hard: requires setting up two equations from two conditions, solving by substitution, and reading the question carefully to return the right variable (hot items, not cold).
